sources.summary: In a slim volume with a yellow-edged cover, recently published by the Porto-based imprint Circo de Ideias , the architect Paulo Martins Barata (a founding partner of Promontório ) makes a deceptively bold claim that the architecture produced in Europe since the Great Recession belongs to neither of the two camps that structured the twentieth century's fiercest disciplinary debate.
